name: Hashrate re-arm with a soft dollar (DXY easing) — miner conviction plus a liquidity tailwind
rationale: A weakening dollar is a classic liquidity tailwind for risk assets including BTC. The thesis combines an external liquidity signal with on-chain conviction: btc_hashrate crosses UP (miners re-arm — structural conviction) AND the dollar is easing (dxy crosses DOWN through a fitted level — a fresh regime change toward looser conditions) AND momentum is positive. Note DXY is treated as a DRIFTING level here and therefore read ONLY via cross_down (a regime-change trigger), NOT a raw lt on its level — this keeps it honest as a change signal rather than a fitted level-in-disguise. btc_hashrate is likewise drifting, used ONLY via cross_up/cross_down. Go long spot. Exit when the dollar firms again (dxy cross_up) or miners capitulate. Disconfirmer (core falsifier): the edge must come from miner re-commitment adding orthogonal info to the dollar-easing trigger. If replacing the btc_hashrate cross_up arm with an always-true pass (keeping dxy cross_down + ret_Nd>0) matches or beats deflated Sharpe, hashrate is redundant and this is just a dollar-easing momentum trade. Low-confidence until OOS; the Gate decides.
catalyst: btc_hashrate crosses up while the dollar (DXY) eases (crosses down) and momentum is positive
